newsitem.title: UK: Defendant in Britain's first war crimes trial dies.
newsitem.headline: Defendant in Britain's first war crimes trial dies.

text.p: A former police commander in Nazi-occupied Belarus who became the first person to stand trial in Britain for war crimes has died in hospital of old age, his lawyer said on Tuesday.
The trial of Szymon Serafinowicz, 86, collapsed in January after eight days when the jury ruled he was not mentally fit to face a full hearing.
He had been accused of being involved in the Nazi programme to wipe out the Jewish population of what was then Byelorussia in World War Two.
The prosecution alleged he had taken part in a massacre in Mir in November 1941 when up to 2,000 Jews, a third of the town's population, were killed.
The jury accepted his lawyers' assertion that Serafinowicz, who denied the charges, was suffering from dementia, probably caused by Alzheimer's Disease, and was not fit to stand trial.
Serafinowicz had lived in Britain since shortly after the war, working as a carpenter until he was 70.
British law was changed in 1991 to allow the trial of alleged war criminals for offences committed outside the country.
But a special police war crimes unit is now investigating only a handful of cases as most suspects have either died or been cleared.
